notes.decision: Translated 'set their hand upon him' as best literal sense. The verbal element ⲩⲝⲧ is unidentified — possibly Lyc. reflex of a 'set/stretch/apply' verb (perhaps ⲡⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'draw out' or ⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'swear/bind'). Idiom ⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ̄ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'his hand upon (someone)' is well-attested for laying-hands gestures.
Read as ⲁ-ϥ-ⲥⲙⲛ̄ⲧ-ϩ '(she/he) established him' (Lyc. perfect with object suffix). The subject is feminine or matches some prior referent in lost context. Perfect of ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ/ⲥⲙⲟⲛⲧ 'establish.'

Translated 'But I — the Anointed who is seated in your midst.' ⲇⲛⲁⲕ ⲁⲉ read as scribal/dialectal variant of ⲁⲛⲁⲕ ⲇⲉ 'But I' (with metathesis). The construction parallels 2 Cor 13:3 (Paul's claim that Christ speaks within him), which fits the apostolic-voice register of this passage.

Translated 'do the work-of-the-doer.' The compound ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲁ(ⲩ/ϩ)ⲓⲣⲉ is the abstract of ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ϩⲱⲃ 'doer/laborer' or related to ⲟⲩⲱⲓⲉ 'farmer' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'the farmer'). Given the immediately preceding seed-sowing imagery (line 10-11), the agricultural reading 'do the farmer's work / labor' is likely. Translated neutrally as 'work-of-the-doer' to preserve the abstract construction. Cf. 1 Cor 15:10 'I labored more abundantly than they all.'

Translated 'a good seedling.' ⲥⲓⲧ = 'sowing, seedling'; ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ likely Lyc. for ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'good' (cf. ⲛⲁϥⲣⲉ in glossary). Alternative: 'seed of the sycomore' (Sah. ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ 'sycomore') is possible but less likely in this paraenetic context. The seed/seedling doublet ⲥⲡⲉⲣⲙⲁ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲥⲓⲧ matches Greek/Coptic agricultural pairings.

Translated 'shall be joined-together with me as fellow-heir.' ϩⲁⲱⲱⲧⲉ likely = ϣⲁ-ⲱⲱⲧ-ⲉ 'shall be joined' (qualitative of ⲱⲱⲧ 'be united, be one') functioning future-modally, paired with the Greek loanword ⲕⲗⲏⲣⲟⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ 'heir.' Alternative: ϩⲁ-ⲱⲱⲧⲉ as preposition + noun. Echoes Romans 8:17 'fellow-heirs with Christ.'

The triple-ⲣⲥ̄ formation in lines 25-27 functions as ornamental chapter-heading framework with the Coptic numeral ⲣⲥ̄ (= 100) as decorative dividers around the title text. Translated each ⲣⲥ̄ literally as '·100·' to preserve the decorative function. The chapter number (100) does not correspond to the actual Kephalaia numbering at this page (which is in the higher chapters), so the ⲣⲥ̄ may be ornamental section-marker rather than literal chapter number.

notes.coptic_form: ⲙⲛ̄ ⲣⲁⲱⲉ ⲉⲱⲁϩⲙⲟⲩⲛ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲃⲁⲗ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ⲩⲁⲃⲁⲗ
notes.decision: Translated 'There is no joy that abides nor any sight in the world forever.' ⲙⲛ̄ as existential negation; ⲣⲁⲱⲉ = ⲣⲁϣⲉ 'joy'; ⲉⲱⲁϩⲙⲟⲩⲛ = ⲉ-ϣⲁϥ-ⲙⲟⲩⲛ 'which keeps lasting/abiding'; ⲙⲛ̄ ⲃⲁⲗ probably 'and (no) eye/sight' as a parallel negation; ⲩⲁⲃⲁⲗ = ϣⲁ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forever.' The chapter-heading sets up the next kephalaion's argument that nothing in the world stands forever, even sun and moon are subject to change.

Translated 'they neither cast a shadow nor know.' ⲑⲁⲓⲃⲉ = ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' verbalized — 'they overshadow / cast shadow.' Negative ⲉⲛ following each verb is the Lyc. circumstantial negative. The double negation continues a series describing what the sun and moon do or fail to do as cosmic luminaries (i.e., they are not autonomous masters but are themselves under summons — line 33).
